articles.text:
LibertyStream Advances Up To $95 Million Financing And Signs New Lithium Sales Agreement
By Amit Chowdhry
Today at 9:32 AM
LibertyStream Advances Up To $95 Million Financing And Signs New Lithium Sales Agreement
LibertyStream Infrastructure Partners has extended its financing exclusivity period with Endurance Finance Partners through January 15, 2027 as the companies continue working toward a proposed financing package of up to $95 million.
Endurance is acting as arranger for the financing framework, which is intended to support LibertyStream’s Freedom 1, Freedom 2 and potentially additional lithium production sites.
The original non-binding financing term sheet was announced on September 3, 2026.
All other terms remain unchanged.
LibertyStream said the additional exclusivity period will allow definitive financing documentation to be coordinated with its broader capital plan.
The proposed financing remains subject to due diligence, investment and credit approvals, definitive agreements, required corporate and regulatory approvals and other customary conditions.
Future project sites would require separate approvals.
The company also disclosed a new commercial agreement supporting its planned lithium production.
On November 4, 2026, LibertyStream entered into a sales contract with a major international cathode manufacturer supplying the U.S. market.
The agreement covers 500 tonnes of lithium carbonate in 2027 and up to an additional 17,000 tonnes between 2028 and 2031.
The 2028 through 2031 volumes remain subject to execution of a long-term supply agreement.
LibertyStream previously entered into a separate offtake agreement in July 2026 with a U.S. industrial customer for 600 tonnes of lithium carbonate annually over five years.
The company is developing technology designed to produce lithium carbonate from oilfield brine.
Its strategy involves deploying proprietary direct lithium extraction technology into existing oil and gas infrastructure, an approach intended to lower capital costs and reduce project development risk.
LibertyStream is working to develop Freedom 1 and Freedom 2 as it seeks to become an early commercial-scale North American producer of lithium carbonate from oilfield brines.
The proposed Endurance financing could provide capital to advance those projects, although LibertyStream said there is no assurance that definitive financing agreements or its proposed Nasdaq listing will be completed.

Israeli Cybersecurity Startup Daylight Raises $80 Million in Series B
The company combines AI agents with human security experts to automate threat detection and response, bringing its total funding to $120 million
Mandi Kogosowski
|
15/11/2026
Sponsored
Illustration: Tima Miroshnichenko via pexels.com
Israeli-founded cybersecurity company Daylight has raised $80 million in a Series B round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, bringing its total funding to $120 million. The New York-based company combines AI agents with human security specialists to detect, investigate, and respond to cyber threats.
The round included new investor Okta Ventures and existing investors Bain Capital, Craft Ventures, Vintage Partners, and Maple Capital. Daylight said its revenue grew more than 40-fold over the past year, driven by demand from Fortune 500 companies and AI-focused businesses. Its customers include Miro, LastPass, Lovable, Rogo, and dLocal.
Daylight's model addresses a growing challenge for corporate security teams: the increasing volume and complexity of threats, alongside difficulties recruiting and retaining experienced cybersecurity professionals. Its platform uses AI agents to handle routine security operations, while human engineers oversee investigations and decisions requiring specialist judgment.
The company offers fully managed and jointly operated services, as well as engineers who work directly within customers' security teams. According to Daylight, its system can detect threats within seconds and contain them within minutes, up to ten times faster than traditional managed security providers.
Its platform also monitors risks associated with enterprise AI adoption, including prompt injection attacks, insecure Model Context Protocol (MCP) connections, and unusual AI-driven activity.
Daylight was founded by Hagai Shapira and Eldad Rudich, who met while serving in an elite Israeli military intelligence unit. Shapira previously held a product leadership position at cybersecurity company Torq, while Rudich was Torq's first employee and vice president of research and development .
The company plans to use the new investment to expand its U.S. operations, enter additional markets in Europe, the Middle East, Africa, and Asia-Pacific, and grow its engineering and technology teams.

Israeli Startup Edelbyte Raises $70 Million to Enter Data Infrastructure Market
Founded by four Microsoft veterans, the company is targeting established players including Snowflake and Databricks as AI drives demand for faster, more affordable data analytics
Mandi Kogosowski
|
15/11/2026
Sponsored
Illustration: Kampus Production via pexels.com
Israeli startup Edelbyte has emerged from stealth with $70 million in seed and Series A funding to compete in the data infrastructure market, targeting established providers including Snowflake, Databricks, and ClickHouse.
Founded in 2025 by four former Microsoft engineers, the company is developing a search and analytics platform designed to help enterprises handle growing data volumes and AI-driven workloads without significantly increasing infrastructure costs.
The funding round was led by Sequoia and Quiet Capital, with participation from Greenoaks and Swish Ventures .
Edelbyte's founders – Avner Aharoni, Evgeney Ryzhyk, Alexander Sloutsky, and Yoni Leibowitz – each spent approximately 20 years at Microsoft, where they worked on Kusto, the data engine used across multiple Microsoft products.
The company is addressing a growing challenge for enterprises: AI applications and agents generate increasing numbers of queries across large datasets, putting additional pressure on infrastructure and budgets. Companies often respond by limiting queries, archiving data, or investing in additional capacity.
Edelbyte says its platform can help reduce these costs while supporting higher query volumes. Some customers migrating from existing systems have reportedly been able to run up to ten times more queries within the same budget.
Despite being founded less than two years ago, the company says it already has Fortune 500 customers running petabyte-scale deployments.
Based in Tel Aviv and San Francisco, Edelbyte plans to use the funding to expand its enterprise customer base, international operations, and workforce.

Remedy Robotics Raises $62 Million Series B to Bring Life-Saving Cardiovascular Intervention to Patients Everywhere
News provided by
Remedy Robotics, Inc.
Nov 16, 2026, 10:00 ET
Share this article
Share this article
Funding will support clinical trials, advancement toward FDA approval, and planned commercial deployment of the company's AI-enabled endovascular robotic platform and software suite
SAN FRANCISCO , Nov. 16, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Remedy Robotics, Inc. ("Remedy"), a leading healthcare and physical AI company developing robotic systems for cardiovascular care and endovascular intervention, today announced it has raised $62 million in Series B funding to accelerate its mission of delivering flawless, immediate robotic care to all patients, regardless of location.
The funding will support several major milestones, including a planned pivotal clinical trial in partnership with the University of California and advancement toward FDA approval for neurovascular intervention. Remedy will also deploy prototype N1 Systems across its network of clinical partners, including through its strategic partnerships with SVIN Mission Thrombectomy and the Australian Stroke Alliance, while continuing to advance the system's industry-leading AI capabilities and autonomous functions.
"Endovascular intervention is the gold standard treatment for stroke and many cardiovascular emergencies, yet access remains limited to a small number of hospitals. For these time-critical conditions, that's devastating. Even when specialist intervention is available, treatment is often delayed, and complications are frustratingly common," said Dr. David Bell, CEO and Co-founder of Remedy Robotics . "This funding will allow us to accelerate toward deployment of our N1 System so we can bring quality intervention to patients everywhere, regardless of geography."
DCVC led the Series B, with participation from new investors including UC Investments (the University of California's investment office), Skip Capital, and Hostplus (one of Australia's largest pension funds). Existing investors Build Collective by Tony Fadell, Blackbird, Divergent Capital and KdT Ventures doubled down.
"Remedy Robotics represents a new generation of medical robotics and physical AI companies, focused not only on technical innovation, but on solving real-world challenges," said James Hardiman, General Partner at DCVC . "We believe the company is uniquely positioned to redefine how life-saving intervention is delivered and are thrilled to support them as they advance toward broader clinical and commercial adoption."
Remedy is finalizing development of the N1 System, an AI-enabled robotic platform and software suite that uses machine learning to analyze preoperative imaging, simulate cases in advance, provide real-time 3D-2D image registration and complete entire endovascular procedures robotically. Designed for on-site, remote, or autonomous operation, the system has the potential to dramatically expand access to and improve the quality of specialized neurovascular, coronary, and peripheral vascular care. Remedy now works with more than 100 hospitals worldwide and is among a small group of physical AI companies bringing robotics into real-world clinical use. In October 2025, Remedy announced that it had successfully completed the world's first remote neurointerventional procedures using the N1 System.

articles.title: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM
articles.snippet: Freshworks alums raise $53M to take on Salesforce, HubSpot with AI-native CRM TechCrunch
articles.text:
Dreamteam , a startup founded by former Freshworks executives, has raised $53 million to challenge Salesforce and HubSpot with its AI-native CRM, betting that AI can finally shake up a market where established players have so far proved difficult to dislodge.
The funding comprises seed and Series A rounds, led by Together Fund and Accel respectively, with participation from Premji Invest. The San Francisco-based startup declined to disclose the size of each round or its valuation.
Traditional CRMs depend on salespeople to manually record customer interactions and keep deal information up to date. That often leaves businesses with incomplete or outdated information. Dreamteam aims to eliminate much of that work by automatically capturing context from sources including emails and customer conversations. It also uses AI agents to handle tasks such as follow-ups, meeting preparation, and pipeline monitoring.
Dreamteam co-founder and CEO Anand Venkatraman (pictured above, right) told TechCrunch that he had repeatedly encountered problems with traditional CRM platforms over more than 25 years in enterprise software, including at Salesforce and Freshworks. Salespeople spent considerable time updating records, yet managers still struggled to get a reliable picture of their business. “In all these years, I have never come across an instance where I could click a button and get a forecast from the CRM,” he said.
That experience led Venkatraman to co-found Dreamteam in 2025 with Senthil Kanthaswamy (pictured above, center), who spent more than nine years at Freshworks, most recently as a product leader at Freshservice, and Ramesh Parthasarathy (pictured above, left), who previously worked on AI and platform engineering at Freshworks.
At the heart of Dreamteam’s CRM is what it calls the Company Brain. This acts as virtual memory, pulling together information from emails, meetings, and other customer interactions to build a shared record of customer relationships. Four built-in AI agents use that information to research prospects, draft follow-up emails, flag potential risks to deals, and configure CRM workflows, with sales teams retaining control over what gets sent to customers.
Dreamteam has signed up more than 100 customers across 13 countries in the three months since it began actively selling its product, with most paying for the service, Venkatraman said. The startup has also replaced established CRM platforms at several businesses, including Salesforce at healthcare company DMS Health and HubSpot at other customers.
The advertising sales team at media streaming company Plex also chose Dreamteam over HubSpot and other AI-native CRM alternatives, Venkatraman told TechCrunch. Plex’s co-founder and chief product officer Scott Olechowski said Dreamteam’s ability to integrate with AI tools already used across the company was a “game changer.”
Replacing established CRM platforms at scale may prove more difficult. In a blog post earlier this year, venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) argued that while AI could transform how businesses manage customer relationships, existing CRMs are likely to remain the systems where customer records are stored, with a new generation of AI-powered tools capturing much of the value by working on top of them.
